title: useMemo, useCallback, useRef and writing a custom hook

videos.script:
Four hooks today, and they are less alike than their names suggest.

{{ref}} useRef is a box React does not watch. It survives every render, and changing it renders nothing. You will use it to reach a real element on the page.

{{focus}} When the course screen opens, the button you pressed disappears, and the keyboard focus falls back to the top of the page. A ref fixes that, and a screen reader user hears where they are.

{{memo}} Then useMemo, which keeps a calculation between renders. Your first attempt will crash, in a way lesson six taught you to recognise.

{{callback}} useCallback is the same idea for functions.

{{custom}} And then the hook you write yourself. App has been carrying two jobs since lesson five. Each becomes a hook with a name, and App drops to half its length.

{{compiler}} Last, the React Compiler, which writes many of these for you, and why you still need to know them.
